member.name: M:WW.Cad.Model.IPathDrawer.IsPreferringSmallFillPaths
member.summary: Is this drawer gaining from small filled paths?
member.remarks: Usually a complete string is draw as one path. Splitting this into single paths for each letter is an order N algorithm (N being the number of letters), so if the drawer works with less effiency depending on the number of paths/points involved (N log N or worse) it should return true here. But be sure to test both cases with a TTF text intensive file because sometimes the memory overhead of creating all new paths eat up the gain.
member.returns: true if this drawer gains from small filled paths, false otherwise

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfEntity
member.summary: Base class for AutoCAD entities (graphical objects like lines, circles etc).

remarks.para: The main properties of an entity are , , , and .

An entity is either in model space or in paper space (see property ). By default an entity is in model space. A model space entity must be part of DxfModel.Entities, a paper space entity must be part of DxfLayout.Entities of the paper space layout on which the entity is shown. The exception to this rule is when the entity is part of a , which can be shown on either model or paper space, depending on if the referencing is in model or paper space. When showing model space (see DxfHeader.ShowModelSpace), entities in paper space are invisible. When showing paper space, entities in model space are first transformed to paper space as specified by a view port. Entities in paper space are not transformed.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfAttributeDefinition
member.summary: Represents an attribute definition that serves as a template for the entity.

remarks.para: Attribute definition visibility is determined by property and DxfHeader.AttributeVisibility. When an attribute definition is part of a block, then the attribute definition is not displayed.

When adding an attribute definition to a , CadLib (upon writing the DXF file) automatically sets the DxfBlock.Flags to include BlockFlags.HasNonConstantAttributeDefinitions so AutoCAD prompts to enter an attribute value when the block is inserted. This happens only in case the block has an attribute definition that is not .

member.remarks: The first alignment point corresponds to the left baseline corner of the text rectangle. This coordinate is redundant for any alignment other than left, baseline. In these cases it can be derived from , , and font characteristics.

member.summary: Gets or sets the second alignment point, optional. In OCS, but after rotation.

remarks.para: The second alignment point location in the text rectangle depends on the and . E.g. if the horizontal alignment is center, then the second alignment point points to the horizontal center of the text rectangle.
The second alignment point should only be omitted if the alignment is left, baseline.

member.summary: Gets the closest entities to specified 2D reference point.
member.param: The graphics configuration object determining aspects like precision.
The reference point to compare with.
The filter delegate to filter out entities to take into consideration (return true to include the entity). When null the default method is used.
member.returns: List of list of entities. Each list represents the chain of entities leading to the target entity. The first item in each list is the target entity, all consecutive items are its parent entities (inserts, dimensions, leaders).
member.remarks: Entities are first transformed by given transformation and transformed points are then compared to given 2D reference point. This method can e.g. be used to get the closest entity to the mouse position.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.Tables.DxfVPort
member.summary: Represents a viewport in model space. Similar to but several DxfVPort objects make up a screen configuration.

remarks.para: The viewport does not need to be unique. Entries with the same name indicate a multiple-viewport configuration. The entries corresponding to the active viewport configuration all have the name *ACTIVE. The first such entry describes the current viewport.
Properties , and optionally the (if is ) determine the transformation to the display coordinate system (DCS).
The viewport's must be greater than zero.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Model.Tables.DxfVPort.Name
member.summary: Gets or sets the viewport name.

remarks.para: The viewport name is not unique. Entries with the same name indicate a multiple-viewport configuration. The entries corresponding to the active viewport configuration all have the name *ACTIVE. The first such entry describes the current viewport.

For and earlier the name may not contain any spaces and may not be longer than 31 characters. Each character of the name should be a letter, digit or one of the following letters: $-_*. This constraint is checked when writing the dxf file by method .

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.ReferenceResolutionType
member.summary: How to handle missing referenced objects when cloning objects from one to another.
member.remarks:
E.g. a entity references a with name "X" that is not yet present in the target model where the entity is cloned to. In that case three options are available to resolve this:
Ignore the missing reference and use the default text style of the target model.
Clone the referenced text style.
Throw an exception when the text style is missing.

member.name: F:WW.Cad.IO.Dwg.EntityType.HasOwnerRelativeRef
member.summary:
The owner relative handle reference is present. Applies to the following: VERTEX, ATTRIB, and SEQEND. BLOCK, ENDBLK, and the defining entities in all block defs except *MODEL_SPACE and *PAPER_SPACE.
Wout, remarks on Viewport:
In R13-14: Only values 1 and 2 are used. In R15: parent handle points to the owner block record, for layout1 value = 1. In R18: it's still used, but only for Layout1 it appears.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.DxfModel
member.summary: CAD model containing a CAD drawing ( objects, and tables).

remarks.para: A CAD model contains entities, which are either in model or paper space. When they are in model space, they are present in the model's collection. If they are in paper space, they are part of the DxfLayout.Entities of the (paper space) layout on which they are displayed.
Entities can be grouped in objects (see property DxfBlock.Entities), which can be referenced by zero or more entities.
Use for reading into a Cad model object.
Use for writing a Cad model object.
Use for displaying a Cad model object.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfHatch
member.summary: Represents a hatch pattern entity.

remarks.para: To define the hatch border, objects must be defined and added to .
There are two types of hatch filling: solid and pattern fill. To create a pattern fill hatch, set property . To create a solid fill hatch, set property to null (the default).
A pattern can be either created from code or by reading from a pattern file (see ).
The object coordinate system is defined by the and .
This entity was introduced in release 14.

member.summary: Point is inside if real y is smaller than or equal to 1.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfMLine.Segment.Element.Parameters
member.summary: Gets the element parameters.
member.remarks: The list may contain zero or more items. The first value is the distance from the segment vertex along the miter line to the point where the line element's path intersects the miter line. The next value is the distance along the line element's path from the point defined by the value to the actual start of the line element. The next is the distance from the start of the line element to the first break (or cut) in the line element. The successive values continue to list the start and stop points of the line element in this segment of the mline. Linetypes do not affect these value.

and when taken as a whole for all line elements in the mline segment, they define the boundary of the fill area for the mline segment.

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfViewport
member.summary: The viewport entity specifies a view in paper space on model space.

remarks.para: A viewport is part of a . The transformation from model space to paper space as specified by the viewport is only applied to entities in model space (see ). Model space entities are part of the model space layout, paper space entities are part of one of the paper space layouts. There may be be zero or more paper space layouts, there is only one model space layout (). Whether a layout is a model space or paper space layout is defined by property .
A viewport is by default in paper space.
The viewport with 1 represents paper space itself and does not show the model.

The defines the position at which the camera is looking in model space. The specifies the direction in which the camera is looking. The defines the view height in model space. The defines the view center in the display coordinate system (the model is transformed to the display coordinate system according to and and optionally the perspective transform). The specifies where the viewport is placed in paper space. Finally the defines the viewport size in paper space.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Model.CellFormat.DecimalNumber.Precision
member.summary: Gets or sets the precision.

remarks.para: For decimal, engineering and scientific units the precision indicates the number of decimals.

For architectural units the precision corresponds to the precision in inches:
value precision in feet/inches
0 0'0"
1 0'0 1/2"
1 0'0 1/4"
1 0'0 1/8"
1 0'0 1/16"
1 0'0 1/32"
1 0'0 1/64"
1 0'0 1/128"
1 0'0 1/256"

For fractional units the precision corresponds to the denominator:
value denominator
0 0
1 0 1/2
1 0 1/4
1 0 1/8
1 0 1/16
1 0 1/32
1 0 1/64
1 0 1/128
1 0 1/256

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Model.CellFormat.Date.FormatString
member.summary: Gets or sets the format string (the default value is null).
member.remarks:
The following sub strings can be used in the date format string.
Sub string Explanation
M month number
d day number
dd day number
yy year number (2 digits)
yyyy year number (4 digits)
dddd day spelled out
MMMM month spelled out
MMM 3 letter abbreviation of month
h hours (0-11)
HH hours (0-23)
mm minutes
ss seconds
tt AM/PM
%#x regional long date: e.g. Saturday, March 29, 2008
%#c regional long date time: e.g. Saturday, March 29, 2008 7:51:24 PM
%x regional short date: e.g. 3/29/2008
%c regional short date time: e.g. 3/29/2008 7:51:24 PM
%X regional time

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Drawing.GDI.GDIGraphics3D
member.summary: Represents a class to draw 3D graphics onto a 2D plane using GDI .

remarks.para:
Usage:
Create intermediate drawable objects (points/lines/polylines) using .
Get bounding box using method .
Calculate the scale transform needed to fit the drawing into the display rectangle using . Set the result with the property.
Draw intermediate drawable objects using .
This intermediate representation is needed to speed up drawing when interacting with the graphics (e.g. rotating, panning, zooming).
2D rendering of and is supported, but not 3D. To disable drawing of image entities set property GraphicsConfig.DrawImages to false.

member.summary: Create drawable objects for given dxf model using given view port.

remarks.para: Old drawables are cleared before creating the new ones.

Entities in model space are transformed to paper space according to the given view ports. Entities that are already in paper space are not affected. Note that the first view port in represents paper space itself and should not be displayed.
These drawable objects are stored and can later be drawn to using the method.

member.param: The layout containing the paper space entities.
The view ports that describe the transformations to paper space. Use to get all the viewports of a layout. If this parameter is null, then all viewports of the specified layout are used.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.IO.PdfExporter.LineWidth
member.summary: Gets or sets the line width.

remarks.para: Quote from the PDF spec: It is a nonnegative number expressed in user space units. A line width of 0 denotes the thinnest line that can be rendered at device resolution: 1 device pixel wide.
Default value is 0.1.

This value is only used if GraphicsConfig.DisplayLineWeight is set to false. Otherwise the normal line weight of the entity is used multiplied by GraphicsConfig.DotsPerInch, times the 100th of mm to inch factor. To choose a proper DotsPerInch value, take into account that the size of a PDF pixel is 1 / 72th of an inch.

member.summary: Gets or sets the line width for text entities.

remarks.para: Default value is 0.1.

This value is only used if GraphicsConfig.DisplayLineWeight is set to false. Otherwise the normal line weight of the entity is used multiplied by GraphicsConfig.DotsPerInch, times the 100th of mm to inch factor. To choose a proper DotsPerInch value, take into account that the size of a PDF pixel is 1 / 72th of an inch.

member.name: M:WW.Cad.IO.PdfExporter.PdfStreamWriter.PdfPathDrawer.IsPreferringSmallFillPaths
member.summary: Is this drawer gaining from small filled paths?
member.remarks: Usually a complete string is draw as one path. Splitting this into single paths for each letter is an order N algorithm (N being the number of letters), so if the drawer works with less effiency depending on the number of paths/points involved (N log N or worse) it should return true here. But be sure to test both cases with a TTF text intensive file because sometimes the memory overhead of creating all new paths eat up the gain.
member.returns: true if this drawer gains from small filled paths, false otherwise

remarks.para: This class serves as a base implementation. In its current form it doesn't do anything, but it's meant to be derived and used as a converter from entities to coordinates of line segment.

To get line segment coordinates of a or e.g. a the following must be done:
Create a object and pass a graphics factory as a parameter to its constructor.
Draw a using method or an using method . Pass the object as a parameter. The model/entity will draw itself on the graphics factory.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfMText.Text
member.summary: Gets or sets the text value.
member.remarks:
This text may contain special processing sequences. Not all possible sequences are supported yet.
Supported processing sequences (note the the char after the backslash should be uppercase):
\ Use the backslash escape for the following characters: \{}~
\Cnnn;
Change color; nnn is the color number.
\P New line.
\FFONTNAME; Replace FONTNAME with the font name (e.g. romant.shx, Arial or Times New Roman). In case of shx fonts it's the font file name, in case of true type fonts it's the font name.
\U[+]nnnn;
DxfInsert a unicode character; nnnn is the unicode character number. If the plus sign is specified then nnnn is hexadecimal, otherwise decimal.
\Hffff;
Set new text height to ffff. Append an x to get a factor from the previous text height. So \H0.7x; reduces the text height to 70%.
{block} Curly braces indicate that the prefixed settings only apply to this block.

member.summary: Gets or sets the reference rectangle width. The default value is zero.
member.remarks: A line break will result when a line exceeds this width, unless this value is zero.

member.name: M:WW.Cad.Model.SurfacePathDrawer.IsPreferringSmallFillPaths
member.summary: Is this drawer gaining from small filled paths?
member.remarks: Usually a complete string is draw as one path. Splitting this into single paths for each letter is an order N algorithm (N being the number of letters), so if the drawer works with less effiency depending on the number of paths/points involved (N log N or worse) it should return true here. But be sure to test both cases with a TTF text intensive file because sometimes the memory overhead of creating all new paths eat up the gain.
member.returns: true if this drawer gains from small filled paths, false otherwise

member.name: T:WW.Cad.Model.Entities.DxfTable
member.summary: The table entity with which tabular data can be represented.

remarks.para: A table has an optional title row and an optional header row (for the column headers). Either one can be suppressed using the and flags. All subsequent rows are data rows. The title row, header row and data row cells have a instances from the associated with them, see , and .

The easiest way to setup a table is to create a DxfTable instance, and set the and . This will populate the and and create instances. Each cell can be accessed through the property. To change a cell's contents, set it's CellFormat and Value.

The table entity has a containing the visual representation of the table data. Whenever a change is made to the table, method should be called to regenerate this block. When the block is not yet generated, it is generated automatically when the is written to file.
The table entity was introduced in AutoCAD 2005.
Currently only by row/column cell styles are supported.

The bottom horizontal line of a double line is interrupted by connecting vertical double lines of the cells below (if they are there). The left and right coordinates are affected by whether the connecting vertical borders are double lines or not.

member.name: M:WW.Cad.Model.WireframePathDrawer.IsPreferringSmallFillPaths
member.summary: Is this drawer gaining from small filled paths?
member.remarks: Usually a complete string is draw as one path. Splitting this into single paths for each letter is an order N algorithm (N being the number of letters), so if the drawer works with less effiency depending on the number of paths/points involved (N log N or worse) it should return true here. But be sure to test both cases with a TTF text intensive file because sometimes the memory overhead of creating all new paths eat up the gain.
member.returns: true if this drawer gains from small filled paths, false otherwise

member.summary: Layer "containing" objects.

remarks.para: An entity is assigned to a layer by setting its Layer property. The layer must be part of the collection.
A layer can be enabled or disabled (see property ). When disabled the entities in that layer are not shown.

Similarly to this a layer can be frozen or thawed (see property ). Its function is almost identical to enabling/disabling, see a more elaborate AutoCAD manual for the differences (or e.g. ). Further more a layer can be frozen in a viewport by adding the layer to .

member.summary: Resolves references for all cloned objects if needed. E.g. e hatch entity may reference a circle entity as its boundary. After cloning both hatch and circle entities, this method will restore these references in the cloned objects. If e.g. only the hatch was cloned, the relation will not be restored.

member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether duplicate names are allowed when cloning. The default value is false.
member.remarks: E.g. duplicate names are allowed, but the user may not intend this to happen.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Model.CloneContext.RenameClashingBlocks
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to rename a block when a block with that name already exists in the target drawing. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When copying a user-defined block from one model to another and there is already a block with the same name, what is about to happen? If this property is true, the block is renamed and copied, if it is false than the block reference of the already existing block with the same name is taken.

member.name: P:WW.Cad.Model.CloneContext.AnonymousBlockMode

member.remarks: When in anonymous block mode, cloned entities are not registered (e.g. dimension BLOCK and their entities should not be registered).
